title: AI assistant for small business owners: daily admin
h1: an ai assistant for the admin around your business
description: A routine pack for customer mail, invoice questions, booking checks and review reply drafts. Start with records you already keep and review the result.
keyword: ai assistant for small business owners
keywords: ai virtual assistant for small business
best ai agents for small business
answer: **you opened a shop, not a second career in inbox admin.** a Metal bot can bring you customer questions, invoice mismatches and tomorrow’s booking gaps from the mail, files and calendar you allow. it can draft replies to reviews you attach too. business use needs a work license. start read only, with answers in chat for you to use.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: customer admin, ready for your decision.

day.what: **see who needs an answer today.** customer messages tied to today’s appointments come first.
**answer from the invoice in front of you.** put the customer’s question beside any amount disagreement.
**draft a review response.** paste the review and keep invented visit details out.
**look at tomorrow’s diary.** flag overlaps and missing details without moving bookings.
**line up receipts with your spending records.** the [receipts sweep](/routines/weekly-receipts-sweep) compares emailed receipts with the sheet you maintain.

pack.name: the opening inbox list
pack.message:
every working day at 8:30, read business gmail since yesterday’s closing time. use hours and policies from the business-rules file in the project folder.

- list today’s customer questions first
- then show supplier questions and deadlines stated in the email
- draft possible answers here
- ask when the rules leave a gap

never send, archive, label or delete mail.
pack.note: **set working days and closing time first.** [email triage](/use-cases/email-triage) covers a fuller inbox setup.

pack.name: the invoice question review
pack.message:
every monday at 10, find unanswered invoice questions in business gmail. compare them with invoices and current payment notes in the project’s invoice-records folder.

show the invoice reference, customer question and any conflicting amount or date here. draft a neutral reply. do not assume silence means unpaid. never contact anyone.
pack.note: **the source is your records, not a bank connection.** [invoice follow-up](/use-cases/invoice-follow-up) covers the related job.

pack.name: the next-day booking review
pack.message: each afternoon at 4:30, read tomorrow’s bookings in business google calendar. flag overlaps or missing service, location or contact details. draft clarification questions here. never send them or move, cancel or create bookings. if the diary is clear, give only the opening appointment time.
pack.note: **calendar read access is enough.** connect the diary that actually holds confirmed bookings.

sections.h: give it the rules customers keep asking about
sections.md:
**stop retyping your opening hours and cancellation policy.** attach the current rules, services and hours. name the version to use and have the bot bring exceptions to you.

keep the first drafts in dusk chat with gmail read only. once the tone is right, allow specific draft actions if saving replies in the mailbox helps. you still decide what the customer gets.

sections.h: a polite reply still needs the facts
sections.md:
**answer the review you received, with the facts you have.** paste it and add the visit details needed to respond. keep private customer information out.

you post the reply yourself in this setup. if the complaint needs investigation, say that. the bot should never invent a phone call, a resolution or a policy exception to make the answer sound better.

sections.h: budget for the business, not the personal trial
sections.md:
**budget for business use from the start.** dusk cloud pro includes a work license for one person; see [pricing](/pricing). your ai provider bills usage separately. free personal use does not cover the shop’s work.

local routines need dusk running on an awake computer. dusk cloud is another home for the bots. keep reviewing bookings normally during the trial; the bot only sees the mail, calendar and records you give it.

faq.q: can i set this up without coding?
faq.a: **yes, describe the job in chat.** make a bot, connect the supported app and ask for a routine. begin with one inbox or calendar you already know.

faq.q: is it free for my business?
faq.a: **no, business use needs a work license.** free local use is personal. ai usage also stays on your provider’s bill.

faq.q: can it chase every unpaid invoice?
faq.a: **give it current invoices and payment records first.** review the proposed follow-up against those records. email silence or a missing receipt alone cannot show who owes you money.

steps: make a bot for customer admin
connect business gmail with read only
attach current hours and cancellation rules
ask for one suggested reply here, with no email sent

worked.intro: invented example: ruth runs a repair shop.
worked.before: a customer asks to cancel tomorrow’s appointment. the old hours sheet and current policy say different things.
worked.after: ruth gets the policy conflict and a draft question in chat. she can settle the cancellation with the current policy in front of her.

checklist.h: before relying on the opening list
items: the hours and policies are current
the connected calendar holds confirmed bookings
invoice answers use current payment records
business use has a work license

mistakes.mistake: treating missing email as an unpaid invoice
mistakes.fix: compare the invoice with current payment records before asking anyone for money.
name the current file and retire conflicting copies from the job.

tip.text: start with the question customers ask every day. you already know what a correct answer sounds like.
